content.question_text: How does the compiler treat ArrayLists with generic type parameters?

core_requirements: The compiler first performs type checking to ensure the type rules are not violated.
After type checking, the compiler erases the generic type information (type erasure).
At runtime, all ArrayLists are treated as raw ArrayList objects (effectively ArrayList<Object>).
acceptable_variations: The compiler removes the generic type after verifying it, resulting in raw ArrayLists at runtime.
Generics are only a compile-time check; the bytecode uses raw types.

content.question_text: What should you be aware of when working with legacy code that uses raw ArrayLists alongside generic ArrayLists?

core_requirements: You will get compiler warnings about unchecked operations due to type differences.
Type safety is lost — the compiler cannot guarantee that the raw list contains elements of the correct type.
This can lead to ClassCastException at runtime if you mix raw and generic types incorrectly.
acceptable_variations: Unchecked warnings and potential runtime ClassCastException.
Mixing raw and generic lists can cause unexpected type errors at runtime.
